item.title: Contemplative Citizenship — Tue Nov 10, 7:00 PM — Saint James Chapel and Zoom
item.description:
Contemplative Citizenship: Lord, make me an instrument of your peace. October 13 – November 10 7 – 8:00 PM in the Chapel In person and via Zoom This Fall, our worship and teaching will be guided by a single line from the Prayer of Saint Francis: “Lord, make me an instrument of your peace.” We will begin this initiative at our Saturday Night Mass on October 3, with local musician and pastor Liz Fulmer leading music that inspires us to embody God’s peace in our lives. On Tuesday, October 13, we will start a 5-week Fall Contemplative Citizenship series in which we will reflect on various lines from the prayer, exploring what it means to embody this prayer in both our personal lives and in our civic responsibilities, especially during this election season when our country feels divided and stressed.

item.title: Evening Compline — Tue Nov 10, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Veterans Day 2026 — Wed Nov 11, 7:00 PM — Garden Spot Village
item.description:
The New Holland Band presents their 3rd annual Veterans Day Concert on Wednesday, November 11 at 7 p.m. in the Chapel at Garden Spot Village. With tunes that reflect the experiences of our servicemen and women, the program will include pop tunes performed by military bands through the years such as “All Shook Up”, “Blue Hawaii”, and “As Time Goes By”. Also on the program is Barber’s “Adagio for Strings” which was used in the movie Platoon. The conclusion of the concert will feature the “United States Armed Forces Service Song Medley” in which we ask veterans to stand and be recognized for their service to our country when they hear their service song played.
The performance on Wednesday, November 11, begins at 7 p.m. in the Chapel at Garden Spot Village. Tickets may be purchased from the band’s website at www.newhollandband.org. item.title: LFS Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons — Sun Dec 13, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Freethought Society **Feminist Film Afternoons #3: The Source (2011)** **What happens when women stop providing what everyone takes for granted?** Join us for the third of five Feminist Consciousness-Raising Film Afternoons, featuring *The Source* (*La Source des femmes*), a French-language drama set in a remote North African village. For generations, women have carried water from a distant mountain spring while men refuse to take on the responsibility. When the women decide they've had enough, they organize a sex strike until the men agree to help provide water for the community. Their withdrawal challenges traditions, relationships, and assumptions about what women owe men.
**After the film, we'll discuss:**
* How does women's unpaid labor sustain unequal systems? * Why is withdrawing cooperation sometimes more powerful than demanding change? * What could women collectively stop providing today—and what might happen if we did?

item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Nov 9, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
